messages:
jen (CS): heads-up: KitePay is reporting repeated 429s and higher tail latency on their dedicated pool (dp-kitepay). They said it started ~10:10 UTC and noticed instances scaling up/down rapidly. raised a support ticket.
oncall-bot: [ALERT] dp-kitepay - 429 rate > 5% over 5m (link to alert) :rotating_light:
mina (SRE): thanks. tenant id + timeframe? i can grab autoscaler logs and pool events.
jen (CS): tenant=kitepay-777, window 10:06 - 10:30 UTC. customer sent snippets showing bursts of 429 then normal.
tomas (Infra): quick flag: logs from similar incidents often show scale-up then immediate scale-down when queue drains too fast -> oscillation. noisy neighbor CPU spike or long-running KV write can cause transient backlog.
mina (SRE): pulling events now. preliminary events: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:11:50Z] pool=dp-kitepay nodes=2 queued=120 cpu=0.88 -> scale up to 6
[2026-03-15T10:12:30Z] pool=dp-kitepay queued=4 cpu=0.22 -> scale down to 3
[2026-03-15T10:13:05Z] pool=dp-kitepay nodes=3 queued=95 cpu=0.81 -> scale up to 7
[2026-03-15T10:13:40Z] pool=dp-kitepay queued=6 cpu=0.18 -> scale down to 2
```
mina (SRE): this is classic snapback. cooldown currently 90s, smoothing window 30s. thresholds: up 0.8, down 0.25.
tomas (Infra): possible compounding: rapid scale up creates more KV contention from new workers warming caches, then requests finish and metric drops -> scale down. also see a bursty tenant on same pool in the past hour (noisy neighbor).
kevin (Prod): customer complaining about extra billing from unexpected nodes. can we short-term set min_nodes=4 to stabilize while we debug?
mina (SRE): yes, we can. my suggested triage steps:
1) temporarily set min_nodes=4 and cooldown=300s for dp-kitepay
2) enable proportional damping (smoothing_window=120s)
3) watch for 429 rate and queue_len for 15m
4) check for heavyweight tenant(s) colocated and consider soft-anti-affinity
(I'll run commands)
jen (CS): customer will appreciate quick minimize churn. they asked about SLA credits — can someone liaise?
liz (Customer): thanks team, we saw a spike in usage but the repeated scale churn spiked our bill. we need an ETA on stabilization.
mina (SRE): running update now: `rbxctl pools update dp-kitepay --min-nodes 4 --cooldown 300 --smoothing 120`
mina (SRE): update applied. scale policy change id=scp-9172. watching.
mina (SRE): after change: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:16:10Z] policy applied scp-9172
[2026-03-15T10:17:00Z] nodes steadied at 4 queued=18 429_rate=0.9%
[2026-03-15T10:22:00Z] queued=8 429_rate=1.2% cpu=0.65
```
kevin (Prod): good. opening billing sync with @billing to review credits for the spike window.
tomas (Infra): next diagnostic: capture flamegraphs / process p99 for any long tail ops on noisy tenant. also check GC logs on new nodes during warmup.
mina (SRE): creating follow-up ticket: INC-2026-1937 with root cause hypothesis: autoscaler hysteresis too low + noisy neighbor causing transient queue spikes. assigning to infra + runtime.
jen (CS): noted. i'll update KitePay with timeline and next steps.
liz (Customer): appreciate the quick response, please ping when stable. :thumbsup:
mina (SRE): follow-up: plan to run a 48h observation, if stable we'll revert min_nodes and tune cooldown to 180s. if churn persists we'll look at tenant placement and hard-anti-affinity.
kevin (Prod): thanks all. action owners: mina (apply config + monitoring), tomas (noisy neighbor investigation), billing (credit review).
jen (CS): closing loop once billing and customer confirm.
note: thread represents support escalation about autoscaling oscillation on dedicated capacity; short messages, logs, and commands included as expected for Slack threads
